selected.assay: whole-blood bulk RNA-seq (PAXgene, polyA, NovaSeq), HISAT2 + featureCounts raw counts, GRCh38 (S2.3.p1)
selected.sample_inclusion: 23 pediatric SCA (HbSS or S/beta0) and 17 age/ethnicity-matched healthy controls with valid RNA-seq both pre and post exercise (S2.1.p1, S3.p1, TAB1); 80 samples

factors.exercise_intensity: 50% vs 70% peak workload, pooled by the authors (S2.4.p1)

selected.repeated_measure_unit: participant (pre and post blood draw from the same child, S2.3.p1); the paper does not state how within-subject correlation was modelled
selected.primary_estimand: acute exercise effect (post vs pre) on whole-blood gene expression within SCA and within controls, and the group x time interaction (difference of the exercise response SCA vs CON)
planned_contrasts: post vs pre within SCA (S3.p1; paper: 391 up + 133 down = 524, P<0.01; Supp Table S2)
post vs pre within CON (S3.p1; paper: 333 up + 290 down = 623, P<0.01; Supp Table S3)
group x time interaction (S2.4.p1, S3.p1; paper: 101 up + 59 down = 160, P<0.01; Supp Table S4)
SCA vs CON at baseline, secondary/non-exercise (S3.p1; paper: 2264 genes, FDR<0.001 and +/-1.50 log2FC; Supp Table S1)
selected.paper_method: limma-voom normalization of raw counts; limma linear models adjusted by sex with a group x time interaction term (limma v3.50.3) (S2.4.p1)

decisions.reason: S2.3.p1 gives assay and GSE244401; S2.4.p1 gives limma-voom, sex adjustment, interaction term, P<0.01 for exercise effects and FDR<0.001 for baseline; S3.p1 gives the DEG counts; TAB1 gives 23 SCA (11M/12F) and 17 CON (12M/5F). The paper does not state whether pairing was modelled (subject block, duplicateCorrelation, or none).

checks: GEO contact Abel Plaza-Florido, UC Irvine PERC = paper group
80 samples = 40 participants x 2 time points; 23 SCA x2 = 46 and 17 CON x2 = 34 match TAB1
metadata sex counts per group (SCA 12F/11M, CON 5F/12M) match TAB1
data_processing: HISAT2 + featureCounts raw counts matches S2.3.p1

decisions.reason: The series is the paper's own deposit and its sample set matches the paper's included participants exactly.

Matrix columns equal metadata title (80/80, inspect alignment_keys). subject = participant code from title (CON02, SCA01, ...); T1/T2 suffix agrees with characteristics 'time 1'/'time 2'; time 1 = baseline (before CIIT), time 2 = immediately after (S2.3.p1).

candidates: raw_counts (confirm against provenance: normalized integers and rounded estimated counts look the same)

decisions.reason: integer fraction 1.0, max 2.1e7, Ensembl gene IDs, 60675 features; GEO data_processing and S2.3.p1 both say featureCounts raw counts.

selected.analysis_type: repeated-measures 2x2 (group between subjects x time within subjects)
selected.formula: within each group: DESeq2 ~ subject + time (paired); interaction: limma on within-subject differences ~ 0 + C(grp) (exploratory); baseline: DESeq2 ~ sex + grp on pre samples

decisions.reason: S1.p4/S2.4.p1: within-group post vs pre and the group x time interaction are the exercise estimands; baseline SCA vs CON is a disease (associational) comparison kept as secondary. Exercise intensity is not a factor because the authors pooled 50% and 70% (S2.4.p1, S4.p7). Post-exercise SCA vs CON is not a paper contrast and is not run.

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: paper adjusts by sex (S2.4.p1); constant within subject, so it cancels in the paired post-pre differences; included as a covariate in the baseline between-group model

decisions.reason: Each participant contributes a pre and a post sample, so the participant is the blocking unit for the exercise contrasts; it is handled by taking within-subject differences (paired change), equivalent to a subject fixed-effect model. Group and sex are between-subject and are not estimable alongside subject fixed effects, which is why the baseline comparison is fitted on pre samples only with sex as a covariate. Sex enters the baseline DESeq2 model as a covariate; intensity is subject-level as well and was left out of the covariate candidates (it is not in the paper's model).

selected.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald), paired ~ subject + time within each group; limma paired-change on log2(CPM+1) for the interaction (exploratory)
selected.formula: ~ subject + time (SCA and CON fitted separately); interaction: delta ~ 0 + C(grp), C(grp)[SCA]-C(grp)[CON]; baseline: ~ sex + grp

paper_route.method: limma-voom with sex-adjusted group x time interaction model
paper_route.reason: tools/limma_voom_tools.py:60 run_limma_voom_analysis is two-group only (no covariates, blocking or interaction) and tools/limma_voom.R:12 uses colSums library sizes without TMM; tools/multigroup_tools.py fits limma on log2(CPM+1) from tools/preprocess_tools.py:111-113, also without TMM. In this whole-blood data globin genes take ~70% of reads in SCA vs ~26% in controls and fall ~2-3 points after exercise, so library-size-only normalization shifts every non-globin gene (first attempt: SCA post vs pre 3923 up / 3 down; baseline 16587 down).

deviations: within-group exercise effects: DESeq2 median-of-ratios (composition-robust) with subject blocking instead of limma-voom

interaction: no composition-robust executor supports subject-nested-in-group plus an interaction; limma on log2(CPM+1) within-subject differences is run and labelled exploratory (expected upward bias in SCA-minus-CON change)
pairing modelled explicitly; the paper does not state its pairing model; sex cancels within subject
baseline: DESeq2 ~ sex + grp on pre samples instead of limma-voom

decisions.reason: Raw featureCounts counts. Whole blood with SCA reticulocytosis: globin read fraction 0.72 (SCA pre) vs 0.27 (CON pre), and it drops after exercise in 34/40 subjects. Library-size CPM (no TMM) therefore inflates non-globin genes after exercise and deflates them in SCA at baseline. DESeq2 size factors (median of ratios) are robust to this and support subject blocking, so they carry the within-group and baseline contrasts. The case-level log2(CPM+1) transform is used only by the exploratory interaction fit.

selected.deviation_note: Exercise rule P<0.01 with no fold-change cutoff (S2.4.p1, S3.p1 'FC ranged from ...' is descriptive). The baseline table has a different paper rule (FDR<0.001, +/-1.50 log2FC); its count under that rule is computed from the result table and reported separately; the applied P<0.01 count for baseline is not comparable.

decisions.reason: S2.4.p1: 'P-value cut-off of 0.01 for exercise effects on gene expression'; audit rule BH padj<0.05 shown for reference.
SCA post vs pre with subject blocking (~ subject + time), composition-robust size factors (S3.p1 Supp Table S2).
CON post vs pre with subject blocking (S3.p1 Supp Table S3).

Only executor that fits the group x time interaction with within-subject pairing: limma on the 40 post-pre differences; group means give within-group effects and their difference the interaction. log2(CPM+1) without TMM biases SCA changes upward, so all three tables are exploratory; the interaction is the one used for comparison with the paper.
Paper's sex-adjusted baseline disease comparison (S3.p1), pre samples only; associational, not an exercise effect.

Paper's voom normalization, without pairing or sex (executor limits); shows how much the pairing and weighting choices move the counts. No TMM in tools/limma_voom.R, so this also shows the composition artifact.
As voom_unpaired_SCA, for controls. No TMM in tools/limma_voom.R, so this also shows the composition artifact.
